scope.title: Policy and semantic review
scope.boundary: Requirement duties that need attributable source inspection or an authorized owner decision. These procedures are review cases, not fabricated executable test methods.

initial_state: Exact release source/candidate, reviewed version intent, relevant engineering assessments and publication observations for the selected routine, exception or incident decision. Record actual reviewed subject identities and assessment limits.

cases.title: Routine eligibility has already approved engineering decisions
cases.risk: Technical green checks substitute for an unresolved engineering or policy decision.

conditions: Select one ordinary release with recorded version intent and supported current population.
For counterexamples remove the version decision, introduce an unresolved contract-breaking change, or request a special release outside routine tooling.

when: Trace package/source changes to the existing engineering decision and version intent.
Assess normal and counterexample packages before approving publication.
then: The supported package identifies its prior decisions and source/version without inventing a release-time engineering decision.
Missing/unresolved authority blocks readiness; a special release records the separate owner decision and is not represented as supported routine execution.

gaps: Routine eligibility has already approved engineering decisions: Perform and record this assessment for the actual release package; synthetic parser tests cannot establish its engineering authority.

cases.title: Exceptional authentication and emergency deferrals have bounded authority
cases.risk: An exception checklist normalizes unsupported or unauthorized routine publication.

conditions: Assess an exceptional manual authentication or emergency release package with synthetic credential references only; compare missing approval, missing rationale/follow-up and attempted deferral of registry identity verification.

when: Identify the owner authorization, fallback reason, exact deferred duty, accepted risk and follow-up deadline.
Check the selected mechanism retains required publication identity and secret protections.
then: Accept only an explicitly authorized exception with all required fields and nondeferrable duties retained.
Reject every missing-authority or forbidden-deferral counterexample; no synthetic case authorizes contacting release services.

gaps: Exceptional authentication and emergency deferrals have bounded authority: Assess the actual exception and authority if one is requested; current local command tests prove only their narrower OIDC and representation boundaries.

cases.title: Recovery from bad published contents preserves the failed public history
cases.risk: A successful retry hides incorrect published contents or silently rewrites release history.

conditions: A published immutable version has incorrect contents or failed public verification. Compare a proposed fix-forward/new version, dist-tag correction or deprecation against a request to republish the same version or erase the failed evidence.

when: Inspect the actual public identity and failure record, proposed recovery scope and owner decision.
Require recorded recovery outcomes and remaining follow-up before considering the incident resolved.
then: Admitted recovery preserves the prior identity and failure history, names the chosen correction and records its actual outcome.
Overwriting the published version, fabricating a prior pass or deleting failed evidence is rejected. No catalog fixture itself executes a public correction.

gaps: Recovery from bad published contents preserves the failed public history: Apply this procedure to the actual incident and its authorized recovery; executor retry tests do not establish fix-forward or deprecation policy decisions.
